enonce_markdown: The order of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\0&5\\4&3\end{pmatrix}$ is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The order of a matrix is written $\text{number of rows} \times \text{number of columns}$. Count the horizontal rows first, then the vertical columns.

### Solution

The matrix has $3$ rows and $2$ columns, so its order is $3 \times 2$.

Wrong options: $2 \times 3$ reverses rows and columns, $2 \times 2$ ignores a row, and $6 \times 1$ counts all the entries as one column.

**Answer: c.**

### Method reminder

To multiply a matrix by a number, multiply every entry by it. To add matrices of the same order, add the entries in the same positions. Do the multiplication before the addition.

### Solution

$2B = \begin{pmatrix}2&4\\-6&10\end{pmatrix}$

$A + 2B = \begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\0&4\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\-6&10\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}5&3\\-6&14\end{pmatrix}$.

Wrong options: $\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\-3&9\end{pmatrix}$ is $A + B$, $\begin{pmatrix}1&-5\\6&-6\end{pmatrix}$ is $A - 2B$ and $\begin{pmatrix}7&0\\-3&13\end{pmatrix}$ is $2A + B$.

**Answer: d.**

enonce_markdown: Given that $A = \begin{pmatrix}2&1\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\5&2\end{pmatrix}$, calculate $AB$ and $BA$. State whether $AB = BA$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

To multiply two matrices, multiply each row of the first by each column of the second: the entry in row $i$, column $j$ of the product is the sum of the products of row $i$ and column $j$ entries, taken in order. Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.

### Solution

$AB = \begin{pmatrix}2&1\\3&4\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\5&2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2(1)+1(5)&2(0)+1(2)\\3(1)+4(5)&3(0)+4(2)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}7&2\\23&8\end{pmatrix}$

$BA = \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\5&2\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\3&4\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1(2)+0(3)&1(1)+0(4)\\5(2)+2(3)&5(1)+2(4)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\16&13\end{pmatrix}$

The two products are different, so $AB \ne BA$.

**Answer: $AB = \begin{pmatrix}7&2\\23&8\end{pmatrix}$, $BA = \begin{pmatrix}2&1\\16&13\end{pmatrix}$, and $AB \ne BA$.**

enonce_markdown: A matrix $\begin{pmatrix}x&6\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$ is singular (it has no inverse). The value of $x$ is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A square matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ has an inverse only if its determinant $ad - bc$ is not zero. It is singular when $ad - bc = 0$.

### Solution

Determinant: $3x - 6 \times 2 = 3x - 12$.

The matrix is singular, so $3x - 12 = 0$, which gives $3x = 12$ and $x = 4$.

Wrong options: $-4$ comes from the sign error $3x + 12 = 0$, $9$ from multiplying the wrong entries ($2x - 18 = 0$) and $12$ from forgetting to divide by $3$.

**Answer: b ($x = 4$).**

enonce_markdown: The inverse of the matrix $M = \begin{pmatrix}3&2\\1&4\end{pmatrix}$ is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The inverse of $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ is $\dfrac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$: swap the entries on the main diagonal, change the signs of the other two, and divide by the determinant.

### Solution

Determinant: $3 \times 4 - 2 \times 1 = 10$.

Swap $3$ and $4$, change the signs of $2$ and $1$:

$M^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{10}\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}$.

Check: $M \times \begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}10&0\\0&10\end{pmatrix}$, which is $10I$.

Wrong options: the second option does not swap the diagonal entries, the third does not change the signs, and the fourth uses $3 \times 4 + 2 \times 1 = 14$ as determinant.

**Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown:
At a market in Douala, $3$ kg of tomatoes and $2$ kg of onions cost $2\,600$ FCFA, while $2$ kg of tomatoes and $5$ kg of onions cost $4\,300$ FCFA. Let $t$ be the price of $1$ kg of tomatoes and $o$ the price of $1$ kg of onions, in FCFA.

(a) Write the information as a matrix equation of the form $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}t\\o\end{pmatrix}= \begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$.

(b) Find the inverse of the $2 \times 2$ matrix.

(c) Hence calculate $t$ and $o$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A pair of simultaneous equations $ax + by = p$, $cx + dy = q$ can be written $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$. If the matrix $A$ has an inverse, multiply both sides on the left by $A^{-1}$: the solution is $A^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$.

### Solution

**(a)** The equations are $3t + 2o = 2600$ and $2t + 5o = 4300$, so

$\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\2&5\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}t\\o\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2600\\4300\end{pmatrix}$.

**(b)** Determinant: $3 \times 5 - 2 \times 2 = 15 - 4 = 11$.

$\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\2&5\end{pmatrix}^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{11}\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\-2&3\end{pmatrix}$.

**(c)** $\begin{pmatrix}t\\o\end{pmatrix}= \dfrac{1}{11}\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\-2&3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}2600\\4300\end{pmatrix}= \dfrac{1}{11}\begin{pmatrix}5(2600)-2(4300)\\-2(2600)+3(4300)\end{pmatrix}= \dfrac{1}{11}\begin{pmatrix}4400\\7700\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}400\\700\end{pmatrix}$.

Check: $3(400) + 2(700) = 2600$ and $2(400) + 5(700) = 4300$.

**Answer: tomatoes cost $400$ FCFA per kg and onions cost $700$ FCFA per kg.**
